data.narrative:
Outrider, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Andrew Smith, has raised $262M to date. The valuation analysis draws on two methodologies triangulated against a comparable universe of five same-sector peers at Series C–E stages, supplemented by a single public comparable.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $262M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $393M. Peer-median analysis references five robotics companies—Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C)—yielding a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.0B–$2.3B. The stage-progression method reflects Outrider's capital efficiency relative to the broader peer set; the peer-median method anchors to direct-stage comparables and accounts for sector-wide valuation levels.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $334M (low) to $1.8B (high), with a median of $996M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty around where Outrider sits relative to Exotec and Hadrian (both Series D peers in the $1.6B–$2.0B band) versus earlier-stage peers. Stage-progression conservatism and peer dispersion—driven by differences in traction, revenue, or market position not captured in stage alone—are the primary drivers of range width.
